requirements.text: WHEN a repo document link inside the open ticket modal is clicked, the system shall open the document in a side pane beside the ticket within the same modal, with ticket content, selected subdocument, and scroll position unchanged.

WHEN a repo document link inside the side pane document is clicked, the system shall navigate the pane to that document and push it onto the pane history (forward stack truncated, consecutive duplicates not pushed).
WHEN the pane back or forward control is activated, the system shall navigate within the pane history and restore the target document scroll position.
WHEN the Escape key is pressed while the pane is visible, the system shall hide the pane and preserve the session (current document, history, scroll positions).

WHILE a session exists and the pane is hidden, the system shall show a reveal affordance naming the current document, and WHEN it is activated the system shall reveal the pane on that document with scroll position restored.
WHEN the pane close control is activated, the system shall discard the session and return the modal to single-column layout.
WHEN the pane hand-off control is activated, the system shall open the Documents view on the pane current document.

WHILE the viewport is narrower than 1100px with the pane open, the system shall present the pane as a full-cover view with an explicit return-to-ticket control that hides the pane keeping the session.
WHEN the Escape key is pressed while the pane is not visible and no trace shell is open, the system shall close the ticket modal as it does today.
All pane controls shall be keyboard-operable with keyboard-only focus-visible rings, and Escape shall walk outward one layer per press in the order trace shell, pane, modal.
Pane content shall render through the same markdown pipeline, theme tokens, and density setting as ticket prose (document prose variant).
The pane shall be a complementary landmark labelled Document preview - {title}, with open, hide, and discard announced to assistive technology.
Outside the ticket modal, document links shall deliver exactly as today (navigation to the Documents view); the pane delivery applies only to links hosted by the ticket modal.
Documents known to be missing shall render flagged and non-clickable, and the pane shall never open for them.
IF a document link is clicked while the pane is hidden, THEN the pane shall reveal on that document pushed onto the kept session history.
IF document navigation occurs in rapid succession, THEN history shall match the committed click order and scroll memory shall not corrupt.
IF the viewport crosses the 1100px breakpoint while the pane is open, THEN presentation shall switch between split and overlay live without losing the session.
IF a pane document target becomes invalid mid-session, THEN the link renders flagged and non-clickable and the current pane document is retained.

IF the pane document fetch fails, THEN the system shall notify via toast and retain any previously loaded document with the session intact; with no previous document loaded, the pane shall show an inline empty error state naming the path.
requirements.sourceRef: CR MDT-248 §4 Edge Cases; UAT r4

requirements.text: WHEN the pane history back or forward control is right-clicked, THEN the system shall show that direction's history entries as menu rows (document title over mono file path) and activating an entry shall jump the pane to it without truncating the history stack.

WHEN a link inside a pane document names a ticket file (authored root-style as {ticketsPath}/{ticket key}[-slug].md, or a ticket subdoc path), THEN the system shall route it to the ticket view (column swap in the modal) instead of the documents world, from any source document.

IF the pane subtree throws during render, THEN the error shall be contained by a boundary: the pane shows an inline fallback naming the ticket as unharmed while the ticket column, modal chrome, and session keep working.

WHEN a ticket or epic link is activated inside the viewer, the system shall replace the main ticket/document in place; same-project navigation shall keep the reference pane unchanged, while a project change shall activate only that destination project's saved reference history.

WHEN a ticket document picker is opened, the system shall show a searchable document tree including Main; selecting a name opens it in that pane and activating its separately labelled Open beside action opens it in the right pane without changing the main document or scroll.

WHILE reading in single, split or fullscreen mode, the system shall keep a compact shared identity header and aligned pane navigation toolbars visible, place priority before the main ticket key, expose Copy path for both documents, identify the right document's source, and offer Trace Graph as an icon only when available.

WHEN the highlighted ticket-details control is clicked or keyboard-activated, the system shall toggle the badge row immediately below the title and remember that state device-wide across tickets, projects and viewer reopen; hover or focus shows a tooltip, not another badge dropdown, and repository documents hide badges without resetting the preference.

WHEN the main pane is closed while two panes are visible, the right document shall become the single main document with scroll preserved; a ticket document supplies its owner's title, key, priority and metadata, while a repository document supplies its own title/path without ticket-only controls; Back shall restore the prior main reading location.

WHEN Fullscreen or Restore is activated, the reader shall toggle between viewport and framed layout without losing documents, selected paths, pane histories, scroll positions or the split preference; Close viewer remains distinct from pane close.

In framed split layout the modal shall be capped at min(94vw, 1560px), use the default main-column width clamp(420px,46%,640px), and allow a persisted draggable divider with a 340px floor per column; below 1100px use an overlay; fullscreen fills the viewport.

Opening, hiding, discarding, promoting, resizing and changing reader header state shall preserve the surviving documents' reading positions; content scrolls beneath pinned chrome and mode changes shall not reset either pane's document or history.

Every document/history/cache identity shall include its owning project and canonical relative document path, plus owning ticket when applicable; storage selection, fetch, link resolution, hand-off, copy and error fallback shall not rebase a document against the currently active left ticket's project.

IF a fetch, cache hit, title/scroll callback or storage write completes after switching projects or promoting a document, THEN it shall not overwrite, display in, or be saved under the new project's reader context.

WHEN Back or Forward is activated in either pane, the system shall restore that pane's visited ticket/document location and scroll independently; main-pane history exists only for the current viewer-open lifetime and resets on close, while only reference sessions persist; these controls represent visit history, not board ordering.

WHEN the reader moves between projects, the system shall preserve a separate project-keyed reference history capped at 50 entries per project, evict oldest entries beyond the cap, restore only the destination project's new-format session, and resolve entries using their owning project; legacy project+ticket snapshots are ignored and never migrated or reinterpreted.

IF the viewer closes, THEN retain only new-format project-keyed reference sessions (50 entries per project, oldest evicted) and restore them hidden on reopening the project; main-pane history resets; right-pane Close clears only the active project's reference session; first r12 load ignores all legacy project+ticket snapshots so each project starts with empty new-format history.

WHEN a repository reference is promoted, the reader shall push /prj/{sourceProject}/read?doc={encodedProjectRelativePath}, preserve current main visit history, and show document-only main mode; in-session browser Back returns to the prior ticket URL, Close replaces the reader URL with that source's Documents-view URL, and direct/reloaded reader URLs open one document with no active reference and no restored main history; existing Documents-view links keep their meaning.

scenarios.title: Document link opens pane beside ticket
scenarios.given: a ticket is open in the ticket modal and its markdown contains a link to a repo document
scenarios.when: I click the document link
scenarios.then: the document opens in a pane beside the ticket inside the same modal, and the ticket column still shows the same subdocument at the same scroll position

scenarios.title: Followed link stays in the pane
scenarios.given: the side pane is showing a document that links to another repo document
scenarios.when: I click that link inside the pane
scenarios.then: the pane navigates to the linked document and the ticket column is unchanged

scenarios.title: Pane back and forward restore scroll
scenarios.given: I have followed two document links in the pane and scrolled the second document
scenarios.when: I press pane back, then pane back again, then forward
scenarios.then: the pane shows each document I visited and each returns to the scroll position I left it at

scenarios.title: Escape hides pane, pill reveals it
scenarios.given: the side pane is showing a document
scenarios.when: I press Escape, see a reading pill naming the document, and click it
scenarios.then: the pane hides without closing the modal, the pill appears, and clicking it reveals the pane on the same document at the same scroll position

scenarios.title: Pane close discards the session
scenarios.given: the side pane is showing a document
scenarios.when: I activate the pane close control
scenarios.then: the pane and the reading pill disappear and the modal returns to its single-column layout

scenarios.title: Hand-off opens the Documents view
scenarios.given: the side pane is showing a document
scenarios.when: I activate the open-in-Documents control
scenarios.then: the app opens the Documents view with that document selected

scenarios.title: Narrow viewport overlays the pane
scenarios.given: the viewport is narrower than the split breakpoint and the pane is showing a document
scenarios.when: I activate the return-to-ticket control and then click a document link again
scenarios.then: the pane covers the modal as a single column, returning hides it onto the pill, and the link re-reveals it with the session kept

scenarios.title: Escape with pane hidden closes the modal
scenarios.given: the pane is hidden and its session pill is showing
scenarios.when: I press Escape
scenarios.then: the ticket modal closes, like it does today when no pane exists

scenarios.title: Right-clicked history control shows a jump menu
scenarios.given: the pane is open with at least two documents in its history
scenarios.when: the back control is right-clicked and a history entry is activated
scenarios.then: the menu lists that direction's entries as title over file path and the pane jumps to the chosen document with the stack intact

scenarios.title: Ticket-file reference routes to the ticket view
scenarios.given: a pane document contains a root-style ticket-file reference
scenarios.when: the reference is activated
scenarios.then: the ticket column swaps to that ticket with the pane session surviving, and no documents navigation occurs

scenarios.title: Same-project ticket navigation preserves the reference
scenarios.given: Ticket A and a reference document are open in one project.
scenarios.when: A related ticket B is followed in that project.
scenarios.then: B becomes main and the reference document, history and scroll remain unchanged.

scenarios.title: Pick and compare internal ticket documents
scenarios.given: Implementation is open and the searchable ticket document picker is visible.
scenarios.when: The user filters for architecture and activates Open beside, then opens review beside.
scenarios.then: The main document stays unchanged; review replaces architecture on the right and Back can return to architecture.

scenarios.title: Pinned headers identify and copy both source documents
scenarios.given: Main shows ticket B and reference shows A/architecture or a repository document.
scenarios.when: Both panes are scrolled and Copy path is used on each.
scenarios.then: Both toolbars stay visible; each copy and provenance names its actual source; priority stays before B's key and Trace targets B only when available.

scenarios.title: Details toggle is remembered across tickets and projects
scenarios.given: Ticket details are collapsed.
scenarios.when: The details control is activated, another ticket/project opened, and the viewer closed and reopened.
scenarios.then: Details remain expanded; a repository document omits ticket badges without clearing the preference and returning to a ticket restores the expanded row.

scenarios.title: Closing main promotes the other ticket document
scenarios.given: Main is A/implementation and reference is B/architecture with a saved scroll offset.
scenarios.when: Close left pane is activated.
scenarios.then: B/architecture fills the reader, header and metadata belong to B, its scroll survives, and main Back returns to A/implementation.

scenarios.title: Closing main promotes a repository reference
scenarios.given: A ticket and a repository document are displayed side by side.
scenarios.when: The main pane is closed.
scenarios.then: The repository document fills the reader with its own title/path, copy and hand-off; ticket badges and Trace disappear and Back can return to the prior main ticket.

scenarios.title: Fullscreen and Restore preserve reading context
scenarios.given: Two documents have independent histories and scroll positions.
scenarios.when: Fullscreen and then Restore are activated.
scenarios.then: The reader frame changes but both documents, histories, scroll positions and split preference survive.

scenarios.title: Project histories remain isolated and resumable
scenarios.given: Project A has a two-document reference history and project B has its own distinct history, including an identically named path.
scenarios.when: The user switches A to B and back, then closes/reopens the viewer.
scenarios.then: Each project exposes only its own history/content/title/scroll and reopens hidden; no A path is requested with B's project identity.

scenarios.title: Main visited locations restore only within one viewer-open
scenarios.given: The main pane visited A/requirements, B/Main and C/architecture with independent reference history.
scenarios.when: Main Back/Forward is used, then the viewer is closed and reopened.
scenarios.then: Main locations/scroll restore before close and main history resets on reopen; only reference sessions restore hidden.

scenarios.title: Legacy snapshots are ignored and each project retains at most 50 references
scenarios.given: Valid legacy project+ticket snapshots exist with no new-format project store.
scenarios.when: r12 initializes and 51 distinct references are visited in project A while B has separate state.
scenarios.then: No legacy path appears; A retains the newest 50 in order, index and metadata stay valid, and B is unchanged.

scenarios.title: Dedicated repository reader supports promotion, deep link, Back and Close
scenarios.given: A ticket plus repository reference is open; an ordinary Documents link is also available.
scenarios.when: The reference is promoted, browser Back/Close exercised, and the read URL opened directly or reloaded.
scenarios.then: Promotion pushes source /read?doc=; Back restores the preceding ticket; Close replaces with source /documents?file=; direct/reload is single document mode with no active reference or main history; ordinary Documents URLs keep opening the workspace.

obligations.title: Document links inside the ticket modal deliver to the side pane with ticket state preserved
Pane navigation uses browser-tab history with per-entry scroll memory
Session states closed/open/hidden with pill reveal and layered Esc chain
Widened split modal with two internal scroll regions and overlay below 1100px
Pane hand-off navigates to the Documents view on the current document
Delivery context defaults inert outside the ticket modal; flagged links never open the pane
Pane renders document prose with theme/density parity and a labelled complementary landmark with announcements
E2E suite locks the pane DOM contract and journeys
Component tests close constraints and edge cases not covered end-to-end
Same-project ticket hops preserve reference; cross-project hops select destination session
Qualify document identity and isolate live state, storage, caches and async results by project
Searchable ticket documents, independent main history, pinned identity and device details toggle
Verify project boundaries, header/navigation and source-safe promotion with deterministic reader regressions
Canonical approved reader specs, interactions and mockups remain aligned; runtime readiness is verified separately
Promotion adopts source identity atomically and uses a dedicated repository reader route with deterministic entry/Back/Close

testPlans.title: Side pane session state machine, chrome contracts, and delivery context
Ticket side reading pane end-to-end journeys
Pane error boundary containment: throwing pane subtree degrades to the inline fallback without unmounting siblings or the app
useToast api is referentially stable across renders (failure-toast loop prevention)
Persisted split-wall percent: round-trip, clear, garbage rejection
Same-ticket, other-ticket and repository headers plus keyboard/narrow access and reference history regression
Project-qualified live history/cache/fetch, DROP legacy snapshots, cap 50 oldest eviction and stale-result isolation
New project-keyed reference store: ignore legacy, empty first use, 50-entry cap, oldest eviction, project isolation, reopen and clear
12a gate: searchable tree, Open beside, per-viewer-open main history and source-correct copy on both panes
12b gate: pinned shared/source header, device details and fullscreen/Restore bound to navigation truth
Source-safe ticket/repository promotion and dedicated reader direct/reload/Back/Close with unchanged Documents links

Esc chain, hide/reveal pill, discard (M2 checkpoint)
Baseline regression closure and final UX-doc reconciliation (r12 adds current target)
UAT r12: isolate project histories, DROP legacy snapshots and cap new histories at 50
UAT r12 navigation truth: picker/Open beside, per-open main history and copy path
UAT r12 chrome: compact header, device details preference and fullscreen bound to navigation truth
UAT r12: source-safe promotion, dedicated repository reader route and final design/regression gate
